criteria.evidence: All 5 style.zoom sites in visual.spec.ts classified inline (commit 32ba25a6): Mission Reading (~L1919) and Work Explorer (~L2450) already honestly named 'CSS zoom stress'/'effective ... CSS zoom stress' with no breakpoint of their own (no @media/@container in their stories.ts) -- left as-is. Repository Dossier (~L2151) has @container (max-width: 720px); measured EMPIRICALLY, not assumed, via a throwaway Playwright probe against the live story: grid-template-columns='322px' identical between style.zoom='2' at 780px width and a genuine halved 390px viewport at deviceScaleFactor:2, both diverging from the 780px-unzoomed baseline ('230.656px 461.344px') -- container queries read local box geometry, which zoom does scale, unlike @media's viewport read -- left as-is, correctly. Reviewer independently re-derived this same result with its own probe (review-cycle-1.md: 'grid-template-columns: 322px' identical both ways) -- two independent confirmations. Connectors (~L2975) claimed unqualified '200% zoom' while its overflow assertion read document.documentElement.scrollWidth/clientWidth, verified empirically unchanged by style.zoom (1440/1440 either way) -- fixed with the same halved-viewport+deviceScaleFactor:2 mechanism as FR-001. Recorded honestly in the code comment and here: no synthetic regression distinguishing the old mechanism from the new one could be constructed (an injected min-width regression was caught by both, since zoom scales injected content too) -- the fix stands on mechanism correctness (the assertion now reads a genuinely narrowed viewport, matching its own name), not on a demonstrated missed bug.
